title: China vows to curb tech bubbles, keep AI risks in check
source_used: Reuters report as carried by Business Standard (Reuters page returned 401); Innovation Village agrees
key_facts: China issued policy guidelines on Friday 9 Oct 2026 on developing 'new productive forces', issued by the ruling Communist Party and the cabinet, as cited by Xinhua.
The guidelines call for breakthroughs in AI theory and core technologies, more supply of computing power, algorithms and data, and national pilot bases for industrial AI applications.
They call for technology monitoring, risk-warning and emergency-response systems so AI remains 'safe, reliable and controllable'.
Officials are told to prioritise the real economy and avoid bubbles, industrial hollowing-out, blind investment and 'swarm-like' rushes into high-tech sectors.
Officials responsible for major losses from blind investment will be held accountable.
China will fully implement its 'AI Plus' initiative, including connected new-energy vehicles, AI phones and computers and humanoid robots.
The document also calls for orderly development of the low-altitude economy (civilian drones, air taxis, small aircraft) while ensuring safety.
quote_evidence: China will tighten oversight of its drive into advanced technology, seeking to curb investment bubbles while ensuring artificial intelligence remains "safe, reliable and controllable", according to policy guidelines issued on Friday.

China will "strictly prohibit the illegal or improper abuse of policies in the name of developing new productive forces," the guidelines said, adding that officials responsible for major losses caused by blind investment would be held accountable.
why_it_matters_hint: Beijing pairs a push for AI self-sufficiency with a warning against wasteful overbuilding.
